lines.text: Sustained human presence in cislunar space relies on propellant management
technologies that either do not exist or exist only at low-TRL. One such low-
TRL technology is propellant mass gauging in microgravity. NASA technology
roadmaps and Artemis architectures call for the ability to measure propellant
in both settled and unsettled states during propellant transfer operations and
during quiescent periods of microgravity. Target gauging resolutions are
typically one percent of full tank volume. As a variety of propellant systems
may be at play in an Artemis mission involving lunar landers, Orion, and the
Gateway Power and Propulsion Element, the ability to gauge both cryogenic
and earth-storable propellant with the same technology is also necessary.
Tank Health Monitoring (THM) is an active vibration based technology which
provides structural integrity information and fluid amount (mass) in tanks in
gravity and zero g environments. The fluid mass application is referred to as
Modal Propellant Gauge. The method is completely non-invasive, is fluid
independent and is highly accurate, providing near real time data.
The Modal Propellant Gauging (MPG) experiment seeks to raise TRL for the
gauging of settled and unsettled propellants from 6-7 by demonstrating an
end-to-end propellant mass gauging system that translates the modal
response of liquid-filled tanks in microgravity to liquid mass measurements

rightsBasis: The NTRS record lists Rudy Werlink, Kennedy Space Center, userType CIVIL, and the page names him as project manager; the data sheet is generated by NASA TechPort (17 U.S.C. 105). The NTRS API copyright record (checked 2026-09-17) gives determinationType GOV_PUBLIC_USE_PERMITTED, containsThirdPartyMaterial false, belongsToPublisher false and licenseType NO; distribution PUBLIC, no export control. Carthage College is named as lead organization in the project data, not as an author of the page. Every page shows the NASA insignia in its header band (14 CFR 1221), and the footer shows the TechPort wordmark. The photos carry no credits: the page-1 sidebar and the page-5 gallery show a lunar-lander render (appearing to be a commercial CLPS lander concept) beside a Gateway render, and the page-5 gallery also shows a slide screenshot with a NASA insignia. The page-3 map, page-2 TRL chart, page-4 signal-chain figure and page-5 formula are NASA project graphics. Owner approved on 2026-09-17. Not relicensed under MIT.
